fields.summary: TC-819-01: Hydration Lambda Returns Correct CoaCrewPairing Object Without Lag When Pairing Data Is Available

content.text: Linked Story: CREWCMBR-819

Precondition: The COA Lag fix for the Hydration Lambda is deployed. Pairing data is already present in the DynamoDB global table when the Hydration Lambda is invoked. The lambda must return the correct CoaCrewPairing object without a lag.
TEST STEPS
Step
Action
Test Data
Expected Result
Ensure pairing data exists in the DynamoDB global table for a specific tripId before invoking the Hydration Lambda
DynamoDB global table: crew-qa2-techp-cmn-coatable with tripId record containing CoaCrewPairing data
DynamoDB global table contains the pairing record for the tripId before the Hydration Lambda is called
Invoke the Hydration Lambda with the tripId for which pairing data exists in the global table
Hydration Lambda invoked with tripId where data exists in global table
Hydration Lambda executes successfully and queries the DynamoDB global table
Verify the Hydration Lambda returns a non-null CoaCrewPairing object in its response
Hydration Lambda response for the tripId
Hydration Lambda response contains a non-null CoaCrewPairing object with correct trip, DP, and leg data
Verify the Hydration Lambda returns null when the tripId does not exist in the global table (lag simulation)
Hydration Lambda invoked with a tripId that does NOT exist in the DynamoDB global table
Hydration Lambda returns null (not an error/exception) - signaling to stream app to retry
Verify the Hydration Lambda response time is within acceptable bounds when data is available (no unnecessary delays introduced by the lag fix)
Hydration Lambda execution duration from CloudWatch metrics
Hydration Lambda completes within expected execution time when data is available - lag fix does not introduce additional latency on the happy path
